Build and restore an R analysis

Keep inputs in _raw_data/ and write results to _output/. With these folder names you can publish a versioned build to GitHub Releases without writing a configuration file, then restore the inputs in a fresh copy of the project.

Get started →Function reference

Run your first build

Open a local clone of a GitHub repository where you can push commits and create releases. Install projr and its publishing tools once, then load the package in R.

install.packages(c("remotes", "gh"))
remotes::install_github("SATVILab/projr@*release")
library(projr)

To install version 0.8.0 specifically, run remotes::install_github("SATVILab/projr@v0.8.0"). To install the current development code, use SATVILab/projr@main. Downloadable source packages

Read an input and write a result

Create _raw_data/measurements.csv with a single column named value and the values 2, 4 and 6. Save the following script as analysis.R in the project root. A production build writes the mean, 4, to _output/mean.txt. The output path helper also lets a development build stage the result in the build cache.

measurements <- read.csv("_raw_data/measurements.csv")
result <- mean(measurements$value)
output <- projr::projr_path_get("output", "mean.txt")
writeLines(as.character(result), output)

Publish a version

Run this in the R console. On the first build, projr shows the checkout’s full path and asks once before running the analysis, writing files and publishing the archive.

projr_build(archive_github = TRUE)

The build creates the starter _projr.yml and uploads inputs and outputs to the archive release. Use a GitHub token with write access to the repository’s contents. People with read access can download the raw data.

For an unattended job started at the checkout root, use projr_build(project = ".", archive_github = TRUE).

Restore the inputs

Clone the same repository into a new folder and open it in R. Run the command below. projr finds the completed build for the checkout and verifies the restored inputs against its recorded hashes.

projr::projr_restore()

To run the production build in a fresh clone and compare the results with the saved files, see Check whether a build reproduces.
